subject: Reserved GPU sizing — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Emma Holt <emma.holt@sapphirehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Reserved capacity conversation — traffic profile attached

Hi Monica,

Great call this morning — thanks for walking through the deployment options. Per our discussion we want to double-check a few things so we can decide between Hosted API vs Reserved (Dedicated) capacity. Attaching our Q2 traffic profile (CSV) so you can see the hourly TPS and token distribution. High level context:

- Primary use case: clinical documentation summaries (long prompts, ~1.2k tokens input, ~600 tokens output).
- Expected steady-state: ~120 TPS during business hours (PST) across a 9am–6pm window; spikes up to ~220 TPS for short bursts (campaigns).
- Percentage of requests that need <100ms median p99 is about 30% (triage UI).
- Security/regulatory: must be VPC-capable; we prefer customer-dedicated tenancy if SLA and throughput are guaranteed.

Questions we flagged in the call:
1) For reserved capacity, what GPU families do you recommend for this token mix (input+output) to hit 120 TPS steady-state with 30% low-latency traffic?
2) How do you handle burst capacity up to ~220 TPS — is burst included or do we need a companion hosted fallback?
3) Concurrency model: how many concurrent requests per GPU do you assume for long-context (1.8k token total) workloads?

Can someone on your side confirm recommended GPU flavor and an initial slot estimate so we can model cost? We're on a tight timeline for procurement next month.

Thanks — Emma
Emma Holt
Head of Platform
Sapphire Health

Hi Emma — thanks for the detailed traffic CSV. Karthik and I ran a quick pass on the numbers. High-level recommendation (rapid sizing estimate):

- Model assumptions we used: 1.8k token total (1.2k in + 600 out), 120 steady-state TPS = 120 completed gens/sec, avg latency per generation on A100-class GPU in our runtime = ~260–320ms depending on batching.

- GPU family recommendation: For large context and predictable p99, we recommend an A100-80GB reserved pool as the baseline. For cost-sensitive mixes, an H100 mix can be used for burst/low-latency lanes but H100 inventory is limited.

- Slot estimate: To hit 120 TPS steady at ~300ms avg per gen, you need ~36 effective slots (120 * 0.3 = 36). Our conservative sizing (accounting for variance and KV caching inefficiencies) recommends starting at 44 slots (reserved) with autoscaling policy to add burst capacity.

- Burst handling: We recommend a hybrid model — reserved pool sized for steady-state (44 slots) + hosted fallback route for spikes above reserved capacity. We can configure automated routing policy to fall back to compatible hosted model (same family quantized variant) to preserve latency. That avoids permanent over-commitment and reduces cost.

- Concurrency: For 1.8k tokens we assume 1 request per slot at p99 targets (i.e., effectively single concurrency per slot for low-latency cohort). For background/async jobs you can pack up to 2–3 concurrent small/short requests per slot.

I can put together a short cost delta (Reserved vs Reserved+Fallback) and a formal slot-by-GPU table if that helps procurement.

Proposed next step: 30-min workshop with Karthik and your SRE to validate the CSV and confirm spike-handling policy. Wed 16th 11:00–11:30am PT or Thu 17th 09:00–09:30am PT work for you?

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
